chapter: Later views and life in Dallas
title: Why the Blue Devils wanted Lester Young
summary: Smith says the band had no hot tenor soloist, wanted hot solos rather than a Hawkins sound, and thought Lester was great.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Why did the Blue Devils want to hire Lester Young, when he was almost the only saxophone player in the world who didn't sound like Coleman Hawkins?
Why was it decided to hire him?

Well, we didn't have no tenor player to get (?). We didn't have no hot tenor player. Reuben Roddy was the main tenor, and he didn't play no solo. No, we didn't have no tenor player at all. See, during them days, tenor players was very popular...
I mean, were you sorry that you couldn't find a tenor player that sounded like Coleman Hawkins?
No. We wanted somebody to be playing hot solos.
And you all thought Lester was great.
